q:
Statement I: A static data member of a C++ class is shared by all objects of the class.
Statement II: A static member function can use the this pointer to access the calling object.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
exp: Static data is shared per class, but static functions have no this pointer.

q: Which technique resolves the ambiguity caused by the diamond problem in C++ multiple inheritance?
exp: Declaring the common base as virtual ensures a single shared base sub-object.

1. Virtual function  2. Friend function  3. Static member  4. Template

exp: Virtual gives run-time polymorphism, friend allows private access, static is shared, template gives generics.

q: In a UML class diagram, a dashed line with a hollow triangular arrowhead pointing to an interface denotes:
exp: Realization (implements) is drawn as a dashed line with a hollow triangle; generalization uses a solid line.

q: Which of the following can access a protected member of a base class in C++?
options: Only the base class, not derived classes
Member functions of the derived classes and of the base class itself
Only objects of the base class created in main
exp: Protected members are accessible inside the class and in classes derived from it.

q:
Assertion (A): Constructors cannot be virtual in C++.
Reason (R): The virtual-table pointer is set up during construction, so the virtual mechanism is not available before the object exists.
options: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
exp: Dynamic dispatch needs the vptr, which the constructor itself initialises, so a virtual constructor is meaningless.

q: Which statement about interfaces in Java 8 is correct?
options: They cannot contain any method body
They can contain default methods with a body

q: Which modifier, applied to a Java class, prevents it from being extended?
exp: A final class cannot have subclasses; abstract classes exist precisely to be extended.

q: The size of the char data type in Java is:

q: Which design principle states that a class should have only one reason to change?
exp: This is the S of SOLID: Single Responsibility.

q: In C++, which data members must be initialised using a constructor member initializer list?

q: In Java, with Parent p = new Child(); p.show(); where show() is overridden in Child, which version runs?
options: Child's version, chosen at run time
Parent's version, chosen at compile time
exp: Dynamic method dispatch uses the actual object type at run time.

q:
Statement I: An abstract class in Java may have no abstract methods.
Statement II: An object of an abstract class can be created with new if it has a public constructor.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
exp: An abstract class can be declared without abstract methods, but it can never be instantiated directly.

q: Which of the following is NOT inherited by a derived class in C++?
exp: Constructors (and destructors, assignment operators, friends) are not inherited.

q: How many arguments does an overloaded binary operator take when defined as a member function of a class?
exp: The left operand is the invoking object, so only the right operand is passed as an argument.

q: A Java member with no access modifier (default access) is visible:
exp: Default (package-private) access limits visibility to the same package.

q: When a C++ try block is followed by catch handlers for both a base exception class and its derived class, the correct order is:
exp: Handlers are tried in order; a base handler first would catch derived exceptions and hide the derived handler.
